title: Discovery document
description: What one set of credentials can see in one platform: a list of resource types, each with whether it could be read and what is there. Written by a `kind: discovery` fetcher, enveloped by the runner like evidence, never uploaded. Platform-agnostic on purpose: one renderer reads every platform's document. See docs/discovery.md.

platform.description: The fetcher category this document describes (knowbe4, aws, ...).

identity.description: Who the credentials authenticated as, in the platform's own terms (an account name, an ARN, a tenant). Null when the platform has no way to say.

scope.description: Where the enumeration looked: region, account, tenant, subscription. Free-form per platform, flat string/number values.

type.description: Singular snake_case name of the resource type (group, training_campaign). Stable: later features refer to resources by this name.

label.description: How a person reads the type name, singular: "EC2 instance", "Security Hub". Optional; the page falls back to the type with common acronyms cased.

note.description: How to read this type's count when the general rules would mislead, e.g. an inventory service that only sees the regions where it is turned on. Shown with the type.

scope.description: Where this entry was listed, when a platform lists the same type in several places: {"region": "us-east-2"}, {"subscription": "..."}. Each (type, scope) pair is its own entry with its own status, so a type denied in one region and readable in the rest says exactly that. Omitted for a type listed once (a global service, a SaaS tenant).

status.description: ok: listed in full. not_enabled: the platform said the feature is off or not licensed. denied: the credentials may not read it. error: anything else, including throttling. denied and error are gaps (we could not tell) and must never be read as 'there are none'. not_enabled is an answer: the platform said the feature is off, so there is nothing of that type to list.

count.description: How many were seen. With truncated: true this is a lower bound. Null when nothing could be read.

truncated.description: True when listing stopped partway, so count and items are incomplete.

items.description: Identifying fields only (id, name, a few attributes), never the full object: discovery says what exists, evidence fetchers say how it is configured. Null for count-only types, which is how a type holding personal data (users) stays out of the document.

summary.description: Small aggregates over the full set, e.g. a count per status. Values are numbers or flat objects of numbers.

reason.description: Why the status is not ok, in the platform's words where possible.

source.description: The call that produced this entry (GET /v1/groups), so a reader can reproduce it.
